claim: When an organization has an organization instance of IAM Identity Center, a member account can create an account instance only if the instance administrator permits creation of account instances (organization instances created after November 15, 2023) or manually enabled it (organization instances created before November 15, 2023). In addition, no service control policy may prevent it, the account must not already have an IAM Identity Center instance in any AWS Region, and IAM Identity Center must be available in the Region.
question: When can an AWS Organizations member account create an IAM Identity Center account instance if the organization already has an organization instance?

qualifiers.condition: an organization instance exists in the organization

evidence.quote: There is an organization instance of IAM Identity Center in your organization and the instance administrator permits creation of account instances of IAM Identity Center (for organization instances created after November 15, 2023).

There is an organization instance of IAM Identity Center in your organization and the instance administrator manually enabled creation of account instances by member accounts in the organization (for organization instances created before November 15, 2023).
After one of the preceding conditions is met, all of the following conditions must be true:
Your administrator hasn’t created a [Service Control Policy](control-account-instance.md) that prevents member accounts from creating account instances.
You do not already have an instance of IAM Identity Center in this same account, regardless of AWS Region.
You're working in an AWS Region where IAM Identity Center is available.
